resolution: Finite validation controls the joint event that a bad predeclared candidate passes under genuine independent sampling from the deployment measure. Online correction instead compares actual mistake counts against a supplied expert budget; neither theorem certifies that its application assumptions hold. The validation bound is not automatically posterior P(good given pass): a fixed bad candidate can pass with positive probability and its bad-pass event equals its pass event. Selection within the predeclared finite pool is covered with its cardinality penalty; selecting an arbitrary memorizer outside it after seeing validation data is not. Accessible justified correction and categorical epistemic authority remain separate open burdens. No finite-risk bound guarantees future truth or closes a root premise.
